items.title: AI Engineer NYC 2026 underway (Oct 12–14) — both Anthropic's and OpenAI's Financial Services product leads keynoting the same mainstage, with Exa and Runway CEOs, Ramp and Modal CTOs, and Wells Fargo's head of frontier models on the lineup
items.summary: The AI Engineer NYC 2026 conference is running October 12–14 at the Sheraton New York Times Square Hotel, with October 13 as the main sessions day following October 12's hands-on workshops (Anthropic and Langfuse among the Monday workshop hosts). The published lineup pairs the product and engineering lead for OpenAI's 'ChatGPT for Financial Services' (launched September 10, 2026 — a GPT-6 Astra-powered variant of ChatGPT Work with built-in Daloopa, PitchBook, LSEG News and Crunchbase data, shaped by a Morgan Stanley and Evercore design partnership) alongside the product and engineering leads for Anthropic's 'Claude for Financial Services' (now shipping Claude Opus 4.7 with 10 customizable agents, Excel/Word integration, and connectors for Third Bridge, IBISWorld, Guidepoint, Dun & Bradstreet, Fiscal AI, and a Moody's MCP server; a separate Claude for Financial Advisors line launched September 15, 2026 with BlackRock, Charles Schwab and Vanguard integrations). The CEOs of Exa (search) and Runway (video), the CTOs of Ramp (fintech) and Modal (compute), and Wells Fargo's head of frontier AI models round out the mainstage. Organizers describe the mainstage track as focused on production AI in financial services, with evals and infra as the second track. The conference is one of the handful of events already in Gabe's `agent/sources.json` list (`AI Engineer` YouTube channel), so recorded talks will likely surface on the channel over the next 1–3 weeks.
items.why_it_matters: The practitioner-conference signal here is that both frontier labs are now in the enterprise-vertical specialization phase — not just selling 'the model' but shipping dedicated product teams, named sub-products, and vertical-specific data integrations for a single industry. For a hobbyist Python developer, that's a useful positioning read even though you're not building against Daloopa or PitchBook: it tells you the frontier-lab product strategy for the next 12 months is 'wrap the model in a vertical, buy the data partnerships, ship an opinionated UI,' not 'release a better general-purpose model and let integrators figure it out.' Three concrete reads: (1) the FinOps/compliance/data-provenance tooling patterns that get battle-tested in the finance vertical first will migrate into every other agent-shipping stack within 6–12 months (audit workflow exports, MCP servers in front of licensed data, Excel/Word integration as the enterprise-UX surface) — those are the patterns worth filing for any Python agent you build that will eventually touch regulated data; (2) 'Claude for Financial Services' running on Claude Opus 4.7 with ten productized agents is a specific template for 'how to productize an agent' that's more concrete than any whitepaper — it's a counting of what one real product-sized bundle of agents actually contains (Excel builder, Word memo editor, data connectors as named integrations, not generic MCP); (3) the AI Engineer channel will carry recordings over the next few weeks, and historically those talks are among the most engineering-dense content of the year — specifically the finance-focused talks tend to be unusually honest about failure modes (reconciliation errors, hallucinated numbers, auditor pushback) because the attendees are the people who have to catch those failures in production. Worth filing the channel for the next few weeks and skimming the talk titles when they drop.
items.why_it_matters_brief: Both Anthropic's and OpenAI's financial-services product leads are keynoting the same mainstage this week — the practitioner-conference signal that the frontier-lab playbook has shifted to vertical-specific product teams with named sub-products, not better general-purpose models.
